niche: Psychology & human behavior (biases, habits, social dynamics)

ideas.title: Why You Feel a Phantom Phone Vibration
ideas.angle: This video explains the sensory hallucination of phantom pocket vibrations through tactile habituation and neural misfires. It surprises viewers by revealing that their nervous system is simply over-predicting sensations due to constant device checking.

hook.en: Your phone isn't vibrating in your pocket.

ideas.reason: It taps into an extremely common modern sensory glitch experienced by almost every smartphone user daily, driving high initial curiosity and instant comments tagging friends.
sources: Computers in Human Behavior journal studies on phantom vibration syndrome

ideas.title: Why Everyone Is Not Staring At Your Flaw
ideas.angle: This video breaks down the psychological Spotlight Effect, demonstrating mathematically and behaviorally how little attention strangers actually pay to our minor wardrobe or social mistakes.

hook.en: Nobody noticed your embarrassing mistake today.

ideas.reason: Social anxiety and self-consciousness are evergreen viral topics. Offering scientific relief from embarrassment consistently drives massive saves and shares.
sources: Cornell University psychological studies on the spotlight effect by Gilovich, Medvec, and Savitsky

ideas.title: Why Too Many Options Make You Miserable
ideas.angle: This video illustrates the Paradox of Choice, showing how adding more options to a simple decision actively decreases satisfaction and causes decision paralysis.

hook.en: More choices actually make you less happy.

ideas.reason: Streaming, shopping, and everyday modern life are plagued by endless options. Viewers instantly relate to feeling paralyzed by menus or Netflix screens.
sources: The Paradox of Choice by Barry Schwartz and related consumer psychology research
